en: He is a man of great courage.
explain: _magnae virtūtis_ is a genitive of description: the adjective _magnae_ agrees with _virtūtis_ (feminine genitive singular), and together they say what kind of man he is.
distractors: Vir magnī virtūtis est.
_magnī_ is masculine or neuter, but _virtūtis_ is feminine. The adjective must agree: _magnae virtūtis_.
Vir magnae virtūtem est.
_virtūtem_ is accusative. A description of a person is a genitive: _virtūtis_.
Vir magnārum virtūtum est.
_magnārum virtūtum_ is genitive plural (“of great courages”). One man has one courage: _magnae virtūtis_.

en: The woman is of great wisdom.
explain: _magnae sapientiae_ is a genitive of description: both words are feminine genitive singular, and they say what kind of woman she is.
distractors: Fēmina magnī sapientiae est.
_magnī_ does not agree with feminine _sapientiae_. Say _magnae sapientiae_.
Fēmina magnae sapientiam est.
_sapientiam_ is accusative. A description is a genitive: _sapientiae_.
Fēmina magnārum sapientiārum est.
_magnārum sapientiārum_ is genitive plural. One woman, one wisdom: _magnae sapientiae_.

en: My father is a man of great glory.
la: Pater meus vir magnae glōriae est.
explain: _vir magnae glōriae_ is “a man of great glory”: _glōriae_ is the genitive of _glōria_, and _magnae_ agrees with it.
distractors: Pater meus vir magnī glōriae est.
_magnī_ does not agree with feminine _glōriae_. Say _magnae glōriae_.
Pater meus vir magnae glōriam est.
_glōriam_ is accusative. A description is a genitive: _glōriae_.
Pater meus vir magnārum glōriārum est.
_magnārum glōriārum_ is genitive plural. One man, one glory: _magnae glōriae_.

en: My book is worth a lot.
explain: _magnī_ is a genitive of value: “of great (value)”. With _sum_ it says what something is worth.
distractors: Liber meus magnum est.
_magnum est_ means “it is big”. For “it is worth a lot”, Latin uses the genitive _magnī_.
Liber meus magna est.
_magna_ is feminine, and it would describe the book’s size. For value, Latin uses _magnī_.
Liber meus magnōrum est.
_magnōrum_ is genitive plural. For value the genitive singular is used: _magnī_.

en: How much is your book worth?
explain: _quantī_ is the genitive of _quantus_ (how much): it asks about worth, as _magnī_ and _parvī_ answer it.
distractors: Quantum est liber tuus?
_quantum_ would ask “how big (a thing)?”. To ask worth, use the genitive: _quantī_.
Quantae est liber tuus?
_quantae_ is feminine, but the question needs the neuter genitive _quantī_.
Quantōrum est liber tuus?
_quantōrum_ is plural. To ask a worth, use _quantī_.

explain: _parvī_ is the genitive of value: “of little (value)”.
distractors: Parvum est.
_parvum est_ means “it is small”. For “it is worth little”, use the genitive _parvī_.
Parvō est.
_parvō_ is dative or ablative. A worth is expressed with the genitive: _parvī_.
Parvōrum est.
_parvōrum_ is genitive plural. For value use the singular _parvī_.

explain: _aestimō_ (I value) takes the thing valued in the accusative (_amīcitiam_) and how much in the genitive (_magnī_): “I reckon friendship at great (value)”.
distractors: Amīcitiam magnum aestimō.
_magnum_ is neuter accusative and would describe a thing. How much you value it is a genitive of value: _magnī_.
Amīcitia magnī aestimō.
_amīcitia_ is nominative. What you value is the object, accusative: _amīcitiam_.
Amīcitiam magnōrum aestimō.
_magnōrum_ is genitive plural. The value is singular: _magnī_.

explain: The opposite of _magnī aestimō_: _parvī aestimō_, “I reckon it at little (value)”.
distractors: Pecūniam parvum aestimō.
_parvum_ would describe a thing. How little you value it is a genitive of value: _parvī_.
Pecūnia parvī aestimō.
_pecūnia_ is nominative. The thing valued is the object, accusative: _pecūniam_.
Pecūniam parvōrum aestimō.
_parvōrum_ is genitive plural. The value is singular: _parvī_.

en: It is not worth that much.
explain: _tantī_ (of so much value) is the partner of _quantī_ (of how much value). Together: _Quantī est? Tantī est._ (How much is it worth? That much.)
distractors: Tantum nōn est.
_tantum nōn est_ would say “it is not so much” (an amount, not a worth). For worth: _tantī_.
Tantō nōn est.
_tantō_ is dative or ablative. A worth is a genitive: _tantī_.
Tantōrum nōn est.
_tantōrum_ is genitive plural. For value use the singular _tantī_.
